series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/1] mm, swap: only prefer nonfull clusters on synchronous devices
series_items.patch_summary: This patch partially reverts a previous change that preferred non-full clusters over free ones for swap allocations on all devices. The new patch prefers free clusters again, except on synchronous devices like zram, where contiguity of slots doesn't matter and filling holes first keeps free clusters available for large folios. This change aims to improve performance by reducing the number of small write requests when rewriting swapped out memory.

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a synchronous device is being used, and suggested adding a check for SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO in swap_prefer_free_cluster() to ensure that nonfull clusters are preferred on such devices.

Reviewer Nhat Pham suggested that it might be beneficial to also prefer non-full clusters for zswap devices, and proposed a possible approach to check the zswap capability of a folio's cgroup.
review_comments.raw_body:
LGTM for the most part:

Reviewed-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>

Quick comment below:

---

Side note - I wonder if it's worth it to also prefer non-full clusters
for zswap as well?

It's a bit tricky, but I suppose you can do a best-effort check of the
folio's cgroup's zswappability?

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Kairui Song questioned whether the patch's logic for preferring free clusters is correct and suggested simplifying it by removing one of the conditions.

Reviewer noted that the new function swap_prefer_free_cluster() is not used in all relevant places, specifically in cluster_alloc_swap_entry(), and requested its usage be extended to cover all cases.
review_comments.raw_body:
I actually wonder if we just want !si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO
here, but still reasonable to keep the two checks here.

---

That's a pretty nice helper, thanks!

The patch itself looks good to me.

Acked-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>

review_comments.author: Alexandre Ghiti
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a synchronous device has both SWP_PAGE_DISCARD and SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO flags set, which would incorrectly prefer nonfull clusters.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti suggested marking the patch as suitable for inclusion in a stable kernel release, citing its previous merge in Linux 7.3.

Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a synchronous device has already been marked as non-synchronous, and requested that the code be updated to check for this condition.

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: The reviewer requested that the patch series be presented as a unified singleton instead of individual patches.
review_comments.raw_body:
Thanks all.

Please avoid single-patch patch series?  Present them as a unified
singleton.

Here's what I ended up with.  Please check.


From: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
Subject: mm, swap: only prefer nonfull clusters on synchronous devices
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:18:32 -0800

Commit 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters") made
the allocator fill nonfull clusters before taking free ones on swap
devices without discard.  Commit 3cedb745d354 ("mm: clarify the
folio_free_swap() for do_swap_page()") frees the swap slot on an exclusive
write fault.  Such faults now leave holes in formerly full clusters,
putting those clusters back on the nonfull list.  Reclaim allocates slots
one folio at a time, scattering a batch across the holes instead of
producing mergeable writes.  Later swapin can also require more read
requests.

On a mysql/sysbench workload in a 256 MiB memcg swapping to an NVMe
partition, 7.3 compared with the previous version produced 59% more device
read requests and 27% more write requests per transaction.  Throughput was
unchanged without iocost and fell 19% with iocost.

Prefer free clusters first on nonsynchronous devices, preserving
contiguous swap slots for merging I/O.  Keep nonfull-first on synchronous
devices such as zram: they do not merge I/O, and filling holes saves free
clusters for large folios.  Keep free-cluster preference on discard
devices to spread writes.

In the same workload, v2 reduced read requests per transaction by 14% and
write requests by 48% against its base kernel.  Throughput was unchanged
without iocost and improved 33% with iocost.  The RFC's batch-aware
allocator also improved this workload, but this policy needs no batch
information from reclaim.  Reverting the slot-freeing change would keep
swap space pinned under dirty pages; a proposed 50% swap-usage cutoff for
free-cluster preference was arbitrary and would stop helping as swap
filled.

The 7.0 to 7.2 kernels retained the swap slot after a write fault as a
side effect of 4b34f1d82c65 ("mm, swap: free the swap cache after folio is
mapped").  The observed regression requires both 9a42aed48421 and
3cedb745d354; stable backports should target trees containing both.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261105155032.240457-1-alex@ghiti.fr
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261105155032.240457-2-alex@ghiti.fr
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261022145615.2184343-1-alex@ghiti.fr
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/CAMgjq7BFbXEKEt9faj_rg5AStfLkpJ0j57EQOOJ+L3-w2xRvtg@mail.gmail.com
Fixes: 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters")
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Suggested-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
Acked-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
Reviewed-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
---

 mm/swapfile.c |   19 +++++++++++++------
 1 file changed, 13 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

--- a/mm/swapfile.c~mm-swap-only-prefer-nonfull-clusters-on-synchronous-devices
+++ a/mm/swapfile.c
@@ -973,6 +973,17 @@ static bool __swap_cluster_alloc_entries
 	return true;
 }
 
+/*
+ * Prefer a new cluster over a nonfull one if the device needs discard, to
+ * spread out the writes, or if it is not synchronous, to keep the slots
+ * of a swapout batch contiguous so that its writes can be merged.
+ */
+static bool swap_prefer_free_cluster(struct swap_info_struct *si)
+{
+	return (si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD) ||
+	       !(si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO);
+}
+
 /* Try use a new cluster for current CPU and allocate from it. */
 static unsigned int alloc_swap_scan_cluster(struct swap_info_struct *si,
 					    struct swap_cluster_info *ci,
@@ -1143,11 +1154,7 @@ static unsigned long cluster_alloc_swap_
 	}
 
 new_cluster:
-	/*
-	 * If the device need discard, prefer new cluster over nonfull
-	 * to spread out the writes.
-	 */
-	if (si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD) {
+	if (swap_prefer_free_cluster(si)) {
 		found = alloc_swap_scan_list(si, &si->free_clusters, folio, false);
 		if (found)
 			goto done;
@@ -1159,7 +1166,7 @@ new_cluster:
 			goto done;
 	}
 
-	if (!(si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD)) {
+	if (!swap_prefer_free_cluster(si)) {
 		found = alloc_swap_scan_list(si, &si->free_clusters, folio, false);
 		if (found)
 			goto done;
_

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance regression in the Linux kernel, specifically related to swap I/O operations on synchronous devices like NVMe partitions. The issue arises from two commits: one that prefers non-full clusters over free ones and another that frees swap slots on exclusive write faults. This leads to scattered writes and increased read requests, resulting in decreased throughput. The patch proposes a solution by only preferring non-full clusters on synchronous devices, which improves performance metrics such as device read and write requests per transaction and throughput.

Reviewer Nhat Pham suggested considering also preferring non-full clusters for zswap devices, noting it would require a best-effort check of the folio's cgroup's zswappability.

It's a bit tricky, but I suppose you can do a best-effort check of the
folio's cgroup's zswappability?

Reviewer noted that the patch is mostly good but suggested keeping nonfull-first only on synchronous devices like zram, which don't merge I/O and where filling holes first keeps the free clusters for large folios.
review_comments.raw_body:
I actually wonder if we just want !si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO

review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch only prefers nonfull clusters on synchronous devices like zram, but this may not be sufficient to address the issue of scattered I/O requests, and suggested reverting commit 3cedb745d354 as an alternative solution.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti suggested the patch should be sent to stable since it was merged in 7.3 and added a Reviewed-by tag.

Reviewer noted that the patch's behavior of preferring nonfull clusters on synchronous devices may not be sufficient, as it does not address the issue of holes in full clusters being filled by reclaim, leading to scattered writes and increased I/O requests.

patches_reviewed.subject: Re: [PATCH v6 05/25] btrfs: zoned: use the regular allocator for conventional metadata block groups
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where replacing a device in a Btrfs filesystem could lead to illegal allocations due to the BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_ZONE flag not being updated correctly. The problem arises when a block group is created on a device with conventional zones and then replaced with a device having sequential zones, causing the system to hang or allocate blocks incorrectly. To fix this, the patch likely updates the allocator to handle such replacements more robustly.

review_comments.author: Johannes Thumshirn
review_comments.summary: reviewer noted that the current implementation of dev replace can lead to illegal allocations when replacing a device from conventional zones to sequential zones, and suggested creating a fstest to catch this issue
review_comments.raw_body:
Oh now I get it. But with that patch set that shouldn't happen anymore 
or at least be way less likely. I agree we need to do something against 
it though. I guess we can make a fstest to catch it: fill the metadata 
by creating a ton of inline extents until we have used up all 
conventional zones and, more to have sth on a sequential zone and then 
do a dev-replace.

I'll try to cook up something.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 0/3] NFS: fixes for delegated timestamps

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 0/3] NFS: fixes for delegated timestamps

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] NFS: don't let delegated c/mtime stamps go backward
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prevents delegated c/mtime stamps from going backward by ensuring that the client's coarse clock does not trail behind the server's fine-grained ctime cached from an OPEN or SETATTR reply. When a delegated stamp is not after the cached ctime, it uses the cached ctime + 1ns instead. This fix addresses an issue where the c/mtime reported by the client while holding a delegation changes after DELEGRETURN, causing problems with file attributes. The patch modifies the nfs_fattr_fixup_delegated function to use a new helper function, nfs_delegated_stamp, which computes the stamp before storing it, ensuring that lockless readers do not see the trailing coarse time.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] NFS: stamp after the server's ctime when truncating under delegated times
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where the client's timestamp can be set before the server's when truncating a file under delegated times. To fix this, it raises the client's cached ctime to match the server's reply time before stamping the delegated timestamp. This ensures that the server's timestamp is always set after the client's. The patch also moves the timestamp update to the same i_lock section as the delegation check and ctime raise, preventing a potential no-op when a delegation return starts during this window.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] NFS: stamp after the server's ctime following a CLONE
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes an issue where the client's ctime is not updated correctly after a CLONE operation in NFSv4.2. The problem occurs when the server stamps its own c/mtime on CLONE, which can result in a newer ctime than the client's coarse stamp. To fix this, the patch passes the CLONE reply's attributes to nfs42_copy_dest_done() and raises the cached ctime to the server's before stamping. Additionally, it applies the reply with nfs_refresh_inode() under delegated timestamps, which doesn't mark ctime invalid. The patch also updates the code to stamp before dropping i_lock to prevent concurrent refreshes from taking the server's times while ctime and mtime are marked invalid.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses issues related to delegated timestamps in the NFS protocol, specifically problems seen in the git regression testsuite. The patches fix four main areas: preventing c/mtime stamps from going backward, ensuring correct timestamping after truncation and cloning, and applying server-side changes under i_lock. The approach taken involves modifying various parts of the NFS codebase to correctly handle delegated timestamps.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 0/8] nfsd: more delegated timestamp fixes

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 0/8] nfsd: more delegated timestamp fixes

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/8] nfsd: Report vetted delegated timestamps in GETATTR replies
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the NFS server where it incorrectly reports delegated timestamps to clients. The issue arises when the server receives a CB_GETATTR reply, which contains raw time_deleg_access and time_deleg_modify values that have not been vetted for validity. These values are then overridden by the server, causing incorrect timestamps to be reported to the client. This patch removes the override, ensuring that only vetted delegated timestamps are returned in GETATTR responses.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/8] nfsd: Honor delegated timestamps when change and size match
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the NFSv4 server where delegated timestamps are not honored when the change and size attributes match. The problem occurs because the holder's WRITEs do not update the mtime or change attribute on the server, causing other clients to see new data with the pre-WRITE mtime. The patch addresses this issue by always applying the CB_GETATTR times for timestamp delegations, recording applied times in the delegation structure, and marking the file modified if necessary. Additionally, it fixes issues related to atime updates and reporting of the stat-based change attribute.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 3/8] nfsd: don't stamp over an applied delegated mtime at DELEGRETURN
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the NFSv4 server where the mtime of a file is overwritten by the current time when a delegated write operation is completed, even if the client has already applied its own mtime. The patch ensures that the mtime is only updated if it passes the ctime check, and sets the ctime to the current time in this case. It also shares the vetting function between SETATTR and CB_GETATTR operations to prevent divergent behavior.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 4/8] nfsd: don't vet delegated times against an exclusive-create verifier
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the NFSv4 server where delegated times are not properly vetted against an exclusive-create verifier. When a client performs an exclusive create, the server stores the client's verifier in atime and mtime until the client sets real times. However, when a delegation is granted on this OPEN, the holder's times are always accepted, including times older than the file itself. The patch introduces a new function to set time floors for delegated timestamps, which uses the ctime as the floor for atime and mtime in case of an exclusive create. This ensures that the server properly rejects times equal to their floor and allows holders to replace the verifier with a time equal to the ctime.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 5/8] nfsd: mark the delegation written on COPY/CLONE instead of stamping c/mtime
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSv4 server to mark a delegation as written on COPY/CLONE operations instead of updating the c/mtime attributes. This change ensures that the client's coarse timestamp does not interfere with the server's ability to update the ctime when the holder returns its times after DELEGRETURN. The patch also removes unnecessary code and updates various functions to handle this new behavior.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 6/8] fs: check a fine-grained time before clamping a delegated ctime
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the inode_set_ctime_deleg function to check a fine-grained time before clamping an update to a delegated ctime. This prevents updates that are past the coarse time but within the same tick as the last reported fine-grained ctime from being clamped back in time, which can cause issues with timestamp delegations. The patch also raises the floor of the update to at least the update itself, ensuring that later coarse stamps cannot land before it. This change affects both multigrain and non-multigrain filesystems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 7/8] nfsd: check a fine-grained time before clamping a delegated mtime
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the nfsd kernel module to check for a fine-grained time before clamping a delegated mtime (last modification time). If the mtime is past the coarse time, it will be clamped against a fine-grained time instead. This ensures that the client's reported changes are not lost when the server's clock is behind the client's clock. The patch also raises the mgtime floor for the file's ctime (last change time) to prevent later stamps from appearing older than they actually are.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 8/8] nfsd: raise delegated time floors after a size-changing SETATTR
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue in the NFSv4 server where a size-changing SETATTR operation does not update the delegated time floors (dl_mtime and dl_ctime) correctly. When a timestamp delegation's stateid is used, the patch ensures that the c/mtime set by the size change is recorded in the delegation's attributes. This prevents stale holder times from moving the timestamps backward and avoids repeated CB_GETATTR replies. The patch fixes a bug introduced by a previous commit (6ae30d6eb26b) and adds support for delegated timestamps.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series, consisting of eight patches, fixes issues related to delegated timestamps in the NFS server (nfsd). The patches address problems that were identified through agentic review and testing with the git regression testsuite. They ensure that delegated timestamps are handled correctly, particularly when change and size match, and fix bugs that caused a new test, DELEG27, to fail against nfsd. The patches also include some minor changes, such as kernel-doc fixes and comment updates.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 0/2] scsi: mpt3sas: Fix delayed not-responding sdev block handling

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 0/2] scsi: mpt3sas: Fix delayed not-responding sdev block handling
[PATCH v3 0/2] scsi: mpt3sas: Fix delayed not-responding sdev block handling

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/2] scsi: mpt3sas: Serialize interrupt-time sdev block with hostdata teardown
series_items.patch_summary: This patch serializes the teardown of hostdata associated with SCSI devices (sdev) to prevent use-after-free issues. It introduces a new lock, ioc->block_lock, which is taken in _scsih_block_io_device() for each sdev and around setting and clearing sdev->hostdata in scsih_sdev_init() and scsih_sdev_destroy(). This ensures that hostdata and its target are live while the lock is held. The patch addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (f92363d12359) and fixes a use-after-free issue.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/2] scsi: mpt3sas: Time out delayed not-responding device blocks
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a deadlock issue in the mpt3sas driver by introducing a delayed work queue to unblock devices that have been marked as not responding after a certain delay. The patch also takes into account both SAS and PCIe device missing delays, and ensures that offline devices are not timed-blocked. This fix is necessary because the previous partial solution did not address all scenarios, particularly when LUN 0 may be blocked before or during a scan.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a deadlock issue in the mpt3sas SCSI driver, which occurs when handling delayed not-responding devices (dnr). The problem is caused by a race condition between interrupt-time blocking and timed unblocking of sdevs. To fix this, the patches introduce serialization mechanisms to prevent concurrent access to shared data structures, including the use of locks and delayed work queues. Specifically, the patches modify the scsih_sdev_init() function to publish sdev->hostdata under a lock, clear block_deadline on all affected sdevs before TUR polling starts, and take the ioc->block_lock in _scsih_block_io_all_device(). Additionally, dnr_unblock_work is deferred while scsi_host_in_recovery(), and mod_delayed_work() is used for retrying. The patches aim to break the deadlock by unblocking sdevs after a timeout, ensuring that the driver can recover from delayed not-responding devices without causing further issues.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 0/4] btrfs: fix FMODE_NOCMTIME handling in btrfs

version_history.subject: [PATCH 0/4] btrfs: fix FMODE_NOCMTIME handling in btrfs

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/4] btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME in btrfs_write_check()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the btrfs_write_check function to honor the FMODE_NOCMTIME flag, which prevents updating the inode's c/mtime when writing files over NFSv4.2. This is necessary because nfsd sets this flag on files with delegated timestamps, and skipping the update ensures that the server's c/mtime does not become newer than the time reported by the delegation holder. The patch fixes a stat-dirty file issue found in git test t1092.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/4] btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME when punching holes
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where Btrfs was updating the c/mtime of files even when FMODE_NOCMTIME was set, which can cause problems for NFS clients holding delegated timestamps. The patch introduces a new function btrfs_should_update_cmtime() to determine whether c/mtime should be updated based on file mode and flags. It then uses this function in btrfs_write_check() and replaces the update_times flag with an argument in btrfs_replace_file_extents(). Finally, it updates btrfs_punch_hole() to skip c/mtime updates for FMODE_NOCMTIME files. This patch fixes a regression introduced by a previous commit that froze c/mtime updates during WRITE_ATTRS delegation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 3/4] btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME in fallocate
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Btrfs file system where fallocate operations would update the inode's ctime and mtime even when FMODE_NOCMTIME is set, which prevents such updates. The patch introduces an 'update_times' flag that is passed from btrfs_fallocate() to its helpers, ensuring that these times are only updated when necessary. Additionally, it increments the inode's i_version unconditionally in btrfs_fallocate_update_isize(), as this operation can change the NFS change attribute even if the size extension stays within existing preallocation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 4/4] btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME when cloning
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Btrfs file system where cloned files would always update their creation and modification times, even when FMODE_NOCMTIME was set. This is problematic because it allows a client to advance the server's ctime during a CLONE operation, which can cause issues with delegated timestamps. The patch makes btrfs_clone_files() respect FMODE_NOCMTIME by passing no_time_update for destinations that have this flag set. Additionally, it exposes the btrfs_should_update_cmtime() function to reflink.c so that it can be used in other contexts.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses inconsistent handling of FMODE_NOCMTIME in btrfs, specifically in write paths and operations like hole punching, fallocate, and cloning. The patches aim to bring btrfs' behavior into line with the generic VFS layer, which suppresses i_version updates when FMODE_NOCMTIME is set.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton
review_comments.summary: Clarified the inconsistent behavior of i_version updates in btrfs, noting that it's a mix of suppressing and incrementing i_version under FMODE_NOCMTIME. Jeff also mentioned that this inconsistency is harmless for nfsd but might be worth addressing for neatness or future use cases.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Mon, 2026-11-09 at 17:10 +0100, David Sterba wrote:
> On Thu, Nov 05, 2026 at 03:07:41PM -0500, Jeff Layton wrote:
> > I tested the delegated timestamp support in nfsd recently. That support
> > relies heavily on FMODE_NOCMTIME, and I found several places where btrfs
> > didn't handle that flag properly. This series seems to fix them for me.
> > I tested mostly with the git regression testsuite, because it is very
> > sensitive to subtle bugs in timestamp handling.
> > 
> > Please consider for v7.5.
> > 
> > Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
> > ---
> > Jeff Layton (4):
> >       btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME in btrfs_write_check()
> >       btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME when punching holes
> >       btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME in fallocate
> >       btrfs: honor FMODE_NOCMTIME when cloning
> 
> There's a comment from sashiko for patch 4 regarding the unconditional
> i_version update but this is mentioned in patch 3 as intentional. I
> can't tell if it's a problem, it seems more like a suggestion for
> cleanup. I'll add the series to for-next, please check if the question
> is valid. Thanks.

Thanks, I think the suggestion from sashiko is a false positive and we
should just merge this set as-is. That said, the kernel _is_
inconsistent in how it treats i_version under FMODE_NOCMTIME:

The generic VFS layer (so ext4, tmpfs, etc.) suppresses i_version
updates when FMODE_NOCMTIME is set.

XFS keeps incrementing it. This is because i_version behavior is a bit
different there (historical reasons). IIRC they more or less keep it in
lockstep with the LSN.

btrfs is mixed -- the write path suppresses it (like the generic VFS
does) but hole punching, fallocate, clone, etc. bump i_version anyway.
This is probably accidental.

In practice, it's harmless for nfsd. While there is a delegation
outstanding, it doesn't consult i_version anyway, and i_version is
updated when the delegation is released.

It might be worth making this more consistent at some point just for
neatness sake though, or in case we want to use i_version some other
way. I'll think about it.
-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's memory management system where migration entries are being treated as partial unmaps, leading to incorrect behavior and statistics. When migrating or splitting large anonymous folios mapped by PTEs, the kernel incorrectly marks them as partially mapped, causing issues with deferred splits, statistics, and folio splitting. The patch introduces a flag to prevent this incorrect marking for migration entries, ensuring that only actual unmappings are treated as such.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/4] mm/huge_memory: scale thp_underused() to the folio size
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the thp_underused() function to make it folio-size-aware, scaling khugepaged_max_ptes_none proportionally to the number of pages in the folio. This change is necessary because a later patch will queue anonymous mTHP folios onto the deferred split list, at which point the current assumption that the folio has HPAGE_PMD_NR pages no longer holds.

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
review_comments.summary: Reviewed the patch and found it acceptable. No specific technical concerns were raised.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Tue, Nov 03, 2026 at 01:20:01PM -0800, Joanne Koong wrote:
> thp_underused() decides whether a large folio on the deferred split list
> is underused and should be split so that its zero-filled subpages can be
> reclaimed.
> 
> Today it only ever runs on PMD-sized folios, so it assumes that the
> folio has HPAGE_PMD_NR pages and compares the zero-filled page count
> directly against khugepaged_max_ptes_none. A later patch will queue
> anonymous mTHP folios onto the deferred split list as well, at which
> point that assumption will no longer hold.
> 
> Make thp_underused() folio-size-aware, and scale
> khugepaged_max_ptes_none proportionally to the number of pages in the
> folio (eg every folio tolerates the same fraction of zero-filled pages
> the user configured for a PMD-sized folio).
> 
> khugepaged deliberately doesn't scale intermediate values when
> collapsing to mTHP orders (to avoid the memory footprint creeping up
> through repeated collapses), but if/when collapse later gains support
> for intermediate values, a folio that khugepaged collapses won't then be
> split right back by the shrinker (and vice versa) since both collapse
> and split would use the same threshold for a given folio size.
> 
> There is no functional change for PMD-sized folios, as for those,
> nr_pages is HPAGE_PMD_NR.
> 
> Suggested-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>

Reviewed-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/4] mm/huge_memory: don't queue folios when underused splitting is inactive
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's huge memory management to prevent anonymous PMD-sized folios from being queued for underused splitting when the system is configured to tolerate any number of zero-filled pages. This change is made by factoring out a check into a new function, thp_underused_never(), which is used in both deferred_split_folio() and thp_underused(). The patch also addresses an issue where folios that were already scanned are not requeued when the sysctl changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/4] mm/huge_memory: add a per-order counter for underused splits
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-order counter for underused huge page splits in the Linux kernel's memory management system. series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 4/4] mm: add anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series adds anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list, addressing memory regressions caused by underused splitting of large THPs on arm64 systems. The change mirrors what is already done for PMD-sized folios and ensures that zero-filled mTHPs can be split and reclaimed when the system is under memory pressure.

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary: Agreed with the hardcoded 2MB minimum size for underused splitting of mTHPs. Provided a Reviewed-by tag.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 5:20 AM Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Unlike for PMD-sized folios, an anonymous mTHP folio doesn't get added
> to the deferred split list at fault or collapse time. As a result, a
> fully mapped mTHP folio that is mostly zero-filled doesn't get split by
> the deferred split shrinker when the system is under memory pressure.
>
> At Meta we would like to deploy 2M THP=always on arm64 with 64k base
> pages, as 2M gives the contpte benefits while the PMD size (512M) is too
> big to use. Without underused splitting this causes memory regressions,
> as the unused parts of those folios can never be broken down and
> reclaimed.
>
> Add anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list from
> map_anon_folio_pte_nopf(), mirroring what map_anon_folio_pmd_nopf()
> already does for PMD-sized folios. This covers both the fault path and
> the khugepaged mTHP collapse path. If there is memory pressure, a
> zero-filled mTHP can then be split with its zero pages remapped to the
> shared zero page and reclaimed.
>
> Only queue mTHP folios of at least 2M for underused splitting. With
> thp_underused() scaling khugepaged/max_ptes_none to the folio size, any
> folio of order 2 or above could in principle be underused, but for small
> folios it is unlikely to be worth it. An order-2 folio on 4k base pages
> can free at most four pages and on systems that only enable small mTHP
> sizes (eg Android's order-2-only configuration) zero-filled subpages
> tend to be few and short-lived.
>
> The minimum is hard-coded rather than a knob, since admins have no good
> way of choosing it, and is a size rather than an order since what a
> split recovers depends on the folio's size in bytes, and the same order
> means very different sizes across different base page sizes. It can be
> lowered later if data shows smaller sizes are worth it. PMD-sized folios
> are exempt from the minimum in order to maintain backwards compatibility
> since on some architectures (s390, with a 1M PMD) the PMD size can be
> below 2M.
>
> To minimize overhead on the common order-0 fault path, the
> deferred_split_folio() call is guarded by an inline folio_test_large()
> check.
>
> Suggested-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
> ---

I believe we discussed this before and agreed that a
hardcoded 2MB would be a better starting point.

Reviewed-by: Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org>
